rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that this verse and those following concern Ṭuʿma ibn Ubayriq: he stole armor and implicated a Jew; his party asked the Prophet to defend him, and he nearly accepted the case against the Jew.
rows.anchor: أجمعوا على أن هذه الآية وما بعدها من أي كثير نزلت في قصة طعمة ابن أبيرق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك، السدي، الحسن، ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd say Ṭuʿma stole the armor and accused the Jew of stealing it.
rows.anchor: والضحاك والسدي والحسن وابن زيد أن طعمة سرق الدرع

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid and Muqatil say Ṭuʿma had been entrusted with the Jew's armor without witnesses, denied receiving it, and accused the Jew of theft.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومقاتل: إن طعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book was sent with truth, meaning on the side of truth rather than falsehood; it can also be called true in the sense that it possesses truth.
rows.anchor: على وجه الحق دون الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's description as al-Haqq in 22:62 illustrates the sense of possessing truth.
rows.anchor: ذلك بأن الله هو الحق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what God showed the Prophet as what God taught him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: "بما علمك الله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other exegetes give the same sense, as when 34:6 uses seeing to mean knowing.
rows.anchor: ومثله قوله: {ويرى الذين أوتوا العلم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that the Prophet's judgment was wholly based on revelation.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل أن رأيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كله وحيا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar warned people not to say they judged as God showed them, since God did this only for His Prophet; the Prophet's view was correct by revelation, while others rely on conjecture and effort.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى لم يفعل ذلك إلا لنبيه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says prophets' judgments are revelation and cites this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: "رأي الأنبياء عليهم السلام وحي"

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rules out eyesight because adjudicating disputes is not perceived by sight, and rules out a form taking two objects, which causative transfer would make take three; the construction instead derives from raʾā meaning to hold an opinion, which takes one object and two after transfer.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: لا يخلو (أراك) من أن يكون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the warning as forbidding the Prophet from litigating for or defending a traitor.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي لا تكن مخاصما ولا دافعا عن خائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṣīm is a disputant, plural khuṣamāʾ; the root refers to an edge or side, whence litigants take opposite sides and a cloud has sides called khuṣūm.
rows.anchor: وخصيمك الذي يخاصمك، وجمعه خصماء

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal's line illustrates khuṣūm as the sides of a cloud that answer each other with thunder; the south wind drives it along.
rows.anchor: قال الأخطل (¬4): إذا طعنت فيها الجنوب تحاملت ... باعجاز جرار تداعى خصومها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, identifies God's favor and mercy as prophethood and protection from sin.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: بالنبوة والعصمة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the favor as prophethood and God's support of the Prophet through revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: بالنبوة، وبنصرك بالوحي

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj take the counterfactual wording to mean the faction did in fact intend and conceal its plan.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء والزجاج: المعنى: لقد همت فأضمرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faction is Ṭuʿma's party: some knew he had stolen the armor but still asked the Prophet to argue for him and blame the Jew.
rows.anchor: لأن بعضهم قد كان وقف على أنه سارق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses their attempt to mislead the Prophet as making him err in judgment.
rows.anchor: يخطئوك في الحكم. قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mislead only themselves by cooperating in sin and aggression and giving false testimony.
rows.anchor: بتعاونهم على الإثم والعدوان، وشهادتهم بالزور والبهتان

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their own actions are the actions of people who have gone astray.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm of false testimony falls on those who testify without right, not on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: لأن الضر على من شهد بغير حق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj attributes the Prophet's immunity from harm to God's protection and support for the true religion.
rows.anchor: مع عصمة الله إياك، ونصرة (¬6) دين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw may begin a new statement of divine favor or introduce a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, as in 4:90.
rows.anchor: قوله: {وأنزل} ابتداء في ذكر المنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is the Quran and wisdom is judgment by revelation.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب: القرآن، وبالحكمة القضاء بالوحي

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says God clarified in the Book its wisdom, which prevents the Prophet from straying.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي بين لك في كتابه ما فيه من الحكمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the brothers as Habil and Qabil: Habil offered his best ram, while Qabil offered poor grain; heavenly fire accepted Habil's offering, not Qabil's, provoking jealousy and the threat to kill. The ram was also said to be the one by which God ransomed Ishmael.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {واتل عليهم} يا محمد

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Unlike the other exegetes, al-Hasan and al-Dahhak say the offerers were two Israelites, not Adam's biological sons.
rows.anchor: إلا الحسن والضحاك فإنهما قالا: إن ابني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary has discussed the meaning of qurban in Surat Al Imran.
rows.anchor: ومضى الكلام في معنى القربان في سورة آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual verb implies that each brother brought an offering, although the noun is singular.
rows.anchor: قرب كل واحد منهما قربانا، نجمعهما في الفعل وأفرد الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurban may be a collective noun that serves for one or many, or a verbal noun like rajahan, ʿudwan, and kufran, formed from a verb meaning to draw near to God by offering property.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القربان اسم جنس، فهو يصلح للواحد وللعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In earlier practice, a person seeking something from God preceded the request with a sacrificial offering; it was called qurban because it brought the offerer near to God, and verbal nouns do not take dual or plural forms.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل فيما مضى إذا رفع إلى الله حاجة قدم أمامها نسيكة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the speaker is elided: the brother whose offering was rejected threatened the other, as context makes clear; Arabic can similarly omit an intended subject in familiar paired situations.
rows.anchor: قاله الفراء (¬1). ومثله في الكلام أن تقول إذا اجتمع السفيه والحليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarraba here means to offer a sacrifice and draw near to God with one's property, not to approach a place or make something physically nearer.
rows.anchor: ليس معناه من القريب الذي هو ضد البعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious are those who refrain from sins; the wording leaves the feared object implicit because sin is what most deserves to be feared.
rows.anchor: فأطلق للعلم بأن المراد أنها أحق ما يجب أن يخاف منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Habil explained that God accepts only from someone pure in heart, and rejected Qabil because his heart was not pure.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: قال له هابيل: إنما يتقبل الله ممن كان زاكي القلب

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس وحذيفة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Hudhayfa explain: if you begin by trying to kill me, I will not be the one who begins by killing you.
rows.anchor: وهذا يروى عن ابن عباس (¬2) وحذيفة (¬3).

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say it was prescribed for people at that time to let an attacker kill them rather than resist.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: إنه كتب عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person defending himself must use the least force needed and aim to repel, not kill; if killing the attacker is the only possible defense, it is allowed, though a victim may choose to submit to unjust death.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل العلم: الدافع عن نفسه يدفع بالأيسر فالأيسر

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: The source says Uthman acted by submitting rather than killing an unjust attacker.
rows.anchor: وكذلك فعل عثمان -رضي الله عنه-

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet instructed Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face with his sleeve and be God's slain servant rather than God's killer.
rows.anchor: أمر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (¬7) محمد بن مسلمة (¬8)

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that one facing a would-be murderer may not raise a hand with the intention of killing; any action must intend to repel.
rows.anchor: فبان أن بسط اليد لقتل القاصد للقتل لا يجوز

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says the slain brother was the stronger man, but scrupulous fear of God kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو في هذه الآية: والله إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as the soul following and complying with him.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: فتابعته نفسه وطاوعته

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad analyzes ṭawwaʿat as a verb derived from ṭawʿ, willing obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: (طوعت (¬4)) فعلت، من الطوع

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the soul as emboldening him; Abu Ubayd explains that it assisted him and answered his wish, deriving the sense from compliance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {فطوعت له نفسه} قال: شجعته

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari considers the likeliest sense to be that the soul made killing his brother easy and tolerable.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: والأشبه عندي أن يكون معنى: (طوعت) سمحت وسهلت

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: On al-Azhari's reading, qatla is accusative directly: the soul portrayed the killing as easy, without an elided preposition.
rows.anchor: فينتصب القتل على هذا من غير إضمار ولا حذف

rows.speaker: الزجاجي
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaji likewise selects making the act easy, deriving ṭawwaʿa from ṭāʿa, to become easy and compliant.
rows.anchor: واختار الزجاجي هذا الوجه فقال: طوع فعل من طاع الشيء يطوع إذا سهل

rows.speaker: الفراء والمبرد
rows.claim: On al-Farra and al-Mubarrad's analysis, qatla is accusative after deleting a preposition, as if the soul complied with killing his brother.
rows.anchor: وأما قول (¬5) الفراء والمبرد فانتصاب قوله: {قتل أخيه}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, says his soul enticed him to kill his brother.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: فسولت له نفسه قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says his soul adorned the killing for him.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: زينت له نفسه

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman says his soul made the killing easy for him.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان (¬2): سهلت له ذلك

rows.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
rows.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says his soul consented to the killing.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى (¬4): أجابته إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says his soul complied with him in killing his brother.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: تابعته نفسه على قتل أخيه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say Cain did not know how to kill; Satan showed him by crushing a bird's head between stones, and Cain later killed sleeping Habil by smashing his head with a stone.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said that for every unjust killing a share of bloodguilt falls on Adam's son, since he was the first to institute murder; Masruq transmits this from Abd Allah.
rows.anchor: وروى مسروق عن عبد الله (¬8) عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali identifies the two who ask to see the ones who led them astray in 41:29 as Iblis and Adam's son who killed his brother, the first to commit disobedience.
rows.anchor: فقال علي: هو إبليس وابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه، كانا أول من عمل بالمعصية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost both worlds: he angered his parents and was left without a brother, and angered his Lord and went to Hell.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد خسر دنياه وآخرته، أما الدنيا فأسخط والديه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes say Cain fled to Aden in Yemen; Satan falsely told him fire had accepted Habil's offering because Habil served it, so Cain built a fire temple for himself and descendants and became the first fire worshipper.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن قابيل لما قتل أخاه هرب إلى عدن من أرض اليمن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in al-Awfi's report, says the verse concerns Abd Allah ibn Ubayy's alliance with Jews and Ubadah ibn al-Samit's disavowal of the Qurayza and Nadir pact in favor of God, His Messenger, and believers.
rows.anchor: فقال في رواية العوفي: إنها نازلة في قصة عبد الله بن أبي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Jews shunned Muslims who had converted; Abd Allah ibn Salam said his people would no longer sit with them, so the verse came and they accepted God, His Messenger, and believers as guardians.
rows.anchor: وقال جابر بن عبد الله: إن اليهود هجروا من أسلم منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account, the verse is general: every believer is a guardian of every other believer, as 9:71 says believers are allies of one another.
rows.anchor: الآية عامة في جميع المؤمنين، فكل مؤمن ولي لكل مؤمن

rows.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak take the description of those who pray and give alms as applying to every believer.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الحسن في هذه الآية والضحاك

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says establishing prayer means completing all its required elements, beginning with sound belief in it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: إقامتها: إتمامها بجميع فروضها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the established prayer as obligatory and the bowing as voluntary prayer by night and day; singling out bowing honors it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {الذين يقيمون الصلاة} المفروضة {وهم راكعون} يعني صلاة التطوع بالليل والنهار

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some semanticists say the believers happened to be in these states when the verse came: some had finished prayer and others were bowing; this assumes a general reading, unlike the specific reading.
rows.anchor: إنهم كانوا في وقت نزول الآية على هذه الصفة

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ikrima's report, says the verse was revealed about Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة: نزل قوله: {إنما وليكم الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, identifies the believers here as Ali ibn Abi Talib.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: {والذين آمنوا} يريد علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Salam says they saw Ali give his ring to a needy person while bowing and therefore declared allegiance to him.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن سلام (¬3): يا رسول الله: إنا رأينا عليا تصدق بخاتمه

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr recounts a petitioner receiving Ali's ring while Ali was bowing; after prayer, the Prophet prayed for Ali to be his minister and support as Aaron was for Moses, then Gabriel brought this verse. The prayer cites 20:25–32 and 28:35.
rows.anchor: فأومأ إليه بخنصره اليمنى وكان يتختم فيها، فأقبل السائل حتى أخذ الخاتم من خنصره

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: In Abu Dharr's account, the Prophet invokes Moses' request for an expanded breast, ease in his task, and Aaron as minister, then asks for Ali as his own minister; the cited verses are 20:25–32 and 28:35.
rows.anchor: فاشرح لي صدري، ويسر لي أمري، واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي، عليا أشدد به ظهري

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: مجاهد، السدي، عتبة بن أبي حكيم، الكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, Utba ibn Abi Hakim, and al-Kalbi say the verse concerns Ali.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد والسدي وعتبة بن أبي حكيم (¬2) والكلبي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the Prophet found a petitioner carrying a ring, asked who gave it to him, and learned it was Ali while bowing; when the verse was read, people understood the phrase about bowing as making the reference specific to Ali.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: أذن بلال فخرج رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - والناس

rows.speaker: أهل العلم
rows.claim: Scholars infer that a small action does not invalidate prayer and that giving alms to a petitioner during prayer is permitted when intended as zakat; the zakat intention does not conflict with prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل العلم في هذه الآية: إنها تدل على أن العمل القليل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Although the occasion of revelation coincided with Ali, the commentators say the verse is general: Abu Jaʿfar Muhammad ibn Ali answers that Ali is included among believers, not the sole referent.
rows.anchor: قال: هم المؤمنون. قلت: فإن ناسا يقولون: هو علي. قال: فعلي من الذين آمنوا

words: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To take God, His Messenger, and the believers as guardians means to undertake obedience to God and support His Messenger and the believers.
rows.anchor: معناه: من يتول القيام بطاعة الله ونصرة رسوله والمؤمنين

words: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those who take these guardians as the Emigrants, the Helpers, and later believers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: "يريد المهاجرين والأنصار والذين آمنوا من بعدهم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is the predicate of the conditional's subject, with its meaning supplying the return to the initial subject; it answers the condition, so it begins with fa.
rows.anchor: جملة واقعة موقع خبر المبتدأ، والعائد إلى الابتداء معناها, لأن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a hizb is a person's companions who share his position; believers are God's party and unbelievers Satan's party.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الحزب في اللغة: أصحاب الرجل الذين معه على رأيه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses hizb as a class or kind of people.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الحزب: الصنف من الناس

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says hizb means a group.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الحزب: الجماعة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses God's party as God's army.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: {حزب الله} جند الله

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another exegete glosses God's party as God's supporters.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: أنصار الله

rows.speaker: أبو روق
rows.claim: Abu Rawq glosses God's party as God's friends.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو روق: "أولياء الله"

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses God's party as His adherents.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: "شيعته"

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash defines God's party as those who follow His religion and obey Him, whom He then supports.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: حزب الله الذين يدينون بدينه ويطيعونه فينصرهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets victory as killing the Jews and expelling them from their homes, while Abd Allah ibn Salam and his companions who allied with God and His Messenger remained.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي في قوله: {هم الغالبون} "فقتلوا اليهود وأجلوهم من ديارهم

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Semanticists offer two readings of the past tense: it may quote what people are told in the Hereafter, as the preceding verse does, or express the future in past form to affirm its certainty.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: (هذا يكون على وجهين أحدهما: أنه على الحكاية

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra calls furada a plural, notes that Arabs also say furadiya, and says it is indeclinable by analogy with thulatha and rubaʿ; its singular forms include fard, farid, fard, and fardan.
rows.anchor: وأما {فرادى} (¬2) فقال الفراء: ({فرادى} جمع

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says fard is something alone; afrad means to make one, and people come furada or count nuts and coins one by one as afrād.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: (الفرد: ما كان وحده، يقال: فرد يفرد

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba parses furada as the plural of fardan, like sukkaran becoming sukara and kaslan becoming kusala.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: (فرادى جمع فردان

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another grammarian derives furada as the plural of farid, on the pattern of radif and ridafa.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: (فرادى جمع فريد مثل رديف وردافى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they come with no family, property, children, or anything they had sent ahead.
rows.anchor: بلا أهل ولا مال ولا ولد ولا شيء قدمتموه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses furada as each person coming alone, separately.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: (فرادى كل واحد على حدة)

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: Ibn Kaysan says they come isolated from what they worshipped and from those who used to support them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان (¬8): (ولقد جئتمونا مفردين مما كنتم تعبدون

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq likewise says each person is separated from his partner in misguidance and accomplice.
rows.anchor: ونحو ذلك قال أبو إسحاق قال: (كل واحد منفرد عن شريكه في الغي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they come barefoot and naked, as they emerged from their mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: حفاة عراة كما خرجتم من بطون أمهاتكم)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj offers another possible sense: just as God began you the first time, so your resurrection is like your creation.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزجاج وجها آخر تحتمله اللغة: (كما بدأناكم أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawwalnakum means gave you ownership; khawl denotes the servants and blessings God grants a person.
rows.anchor: أي: ملكناكم، يقال: خوله الشيء

rows.speaker: أبو النجم
rows.claim: Abu al-Najm's phrase kom al-dhura min khawl al-mukhawwil supplies poetic evidence for khawl as a grant or possession.
rows.anchor: قال أبو النجم (¬6): كوم الذرى من خول المخول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas specifies the abandoned gifts as comforts, wealth, servants, estates, and livestock.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {وتركتم ما خولناكم}: (يريد: من النعيم والمال

words: شُفَعَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكَآءُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the idols were alleged partners of God; exegetes explain that polytheists worshipped them as God's partners and intercessors with Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: شركاء لي) (¬3) و {شفعاءكم}، قال المفسرون (¬4):

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the nominative baynu-kum, meaning the bond between you broke; the accusative is also allowed and means your association was severed.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬5): (الرفع (¬6) أجود، [و] (¬7) معناه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says bayn can be a declinable noun or an adverb; the nominative reading treats the adverb as a noun, supported by its use in 41:5 and 18:78 and in Muhalhil's line. It cannot be a verbal noun meaning separation, since that would yield the wrong sense of 'your separation has separated.'
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: (هذا الاسم يستعمل على ضربين: أحدهما: أن يكون اسما متصرفا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains the shift: between people who share kinship, friendship, or partnership can function like a bond, so its severance means their bond has broken; Sibawayh's example also supports nominal use.
rows.anchor: لما استعمل مع الشيئين المتلابسين في نحو: بيني وبينه شركة

rows.speaker: مهلهل
rows.claim: Muhalhil's poem uses bayn as a noun for the distance between the two sides of a well, supporting Abu Ali's grammatical analysis.
rows.anchor: وقال (¬2) مهلهل (¬3): كأن رماحهم أشطان بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis of the accusative reading supplies an omitted subject from the preceding mention of alleged partners: their bond among you has been severed.
rows.anchor: فأما من قرأ: {لقد تقطع بينكم} بالنصب ففيه مذهبان أحدهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses what has broken between them as their bond and affection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {لقد تقطع بينكم} (يريد: وصلكم ومودتكم)

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says the relations they maintained with one another have ended.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {لقد تقطع بينكم} (يعني: ما تواصلتم بينكم)

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as the matter between them having been broken off.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: (لقد تقطع الأمر بينكم)

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it means whatever bond existed between them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: (ما بينكم من الوصل)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their claims have vanished: what they used to lie about in worldly life is gone.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (ذهب عنكم ما كنتم تكذبون في الدنيا)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes 'We created you' to mean Adam, and 'then shaped you' to mean his descendants.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أما {خلقناكم} فآدم (¬2)، وأما {صورناكم}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid likewise says Adam was created and his descendants were shaped in Adam's back.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد: ({خلقناكم} يعني: آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'We created you' can refer to Adam because he is the father of humankind and his creation included descendants who would emerge from his loins.
rows.anchor: لأنه أبو البشر وفي خلقه خلق يخرج من صلبه

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus says 'then We shaped you' may refer to Adam alone, just as a plural expression can refer to a people's chief.
rows.anchor: وهو قول يونس (¬7)، قال: (يجوز أن يكون معنى {صورناكم} لآدم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd prefers Mujahid's interpretation, citing what follows in the verse; the excerpt ends before his evidence is given.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد (¬10) في هذه الآية قول مجاهد لقوله بعده
